title: Wound Care Supply Program Enrollment and Tier Assignment
content:
# Enrollment and tier assignment — Wound Care Supply Program

Benefits verification policy for opening a wound care program and for writing its coverage and tier.

## Clauses

1. **Opening.** A wound care program is opened when Larkfield accepts a referral for the Wound Care Supply Program; the program opens in referral received status, bound to the coverage it will bill. The tier written on the program is fixed by the coverage the program bills, never by the customer's preference.
2. **Locating the tier.** The tier is located from the coverage record named on the program: the coverage record's plan type and coverage order must equal the tier's entry gate, and the Wound Care Self-Pay Program is used only when no coverage record is named.
3. **Coverage in effect.** The coverage record named on the program must be in effect on the date of the write: its effective date is on or before that date and its termination date is empty or on or after that date. This applies both when a program is opened and when a program change writes a coverage onto it, and it is read from the coverage record on file.
4. **Original Medicare beneficiaries.** A customer with an in-effect Original Medicare Part B coverage record cannot be enrolled on the Wound Care Self-Pay Program for an item Medicare covers, because Larkfield submits a claim for every Medicare-covered item it supplies to a Medicare beneficiary; that customer is enrolled on the Wound Care Original Medicare Program, and an item or quantity Medicare will not pay is handled under the program's advance notice of financial liability rules.
5. **Two coverages.** When a customer has two in-effect coverage records, the one whose coverage order is primary fixes the tier and the secondary coverage only receives crossover or secondary claims; a coverage record whose coverage order is secondary never fixes the tier.
6. **Clinical qualification.** Any clinical qualification in the tier's entry gate is read from the program's own clinical fields as documented on the prescriber's written order and medical records, never from the customer's description alone.
7. **Program changes.** A program change rewrites the coverage reference and the tier together when the customer's insurance changes, and rewrites prescriber or product fields when a newer written order changes them; a change never rewrites status, and after a tier change the next refill may draw only on an authorization grant recorded under the new tier.
8. **Coverage not on file.** A coverage the customer reports that is not on file cannot be written onto a program, because coverage records are created only by Larkfield's benefits verification team after the payer confirms eligibility.

## Coverage in effect on the date of the write (hypothetical write date 2026-03-01)

| Effective date | Termination date | In effect on 2026-03-01 |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-03-01 | empty | Yes — effective on the date of the write |
| 2026-03-02 | empty | No — effective date is after the date of the write |
| 2025-01-01 | 2026-03-01 | Yes — terminates on the date of the write |
| 2025-01-01 | 2026-02-28 | No — terminated before the date of the write |

## What the records show and what the customer says

- The coverage, its plan type, its coverage order and its dates come from the coverage record on file. A plan the customer describes but that has no coverage record on file is not written onto a program.
- The clinical qualification comes from the written order and the medical records on the program, not from the customer's account of the wound.

## Points of judgement

- *A customer holds an in-effect primary commercial PPO coverage record and an in-effect secondary Medicaid coverage record. Which coverage fixes the tier?* The primary commercial PPO record; the program is on the Wound Care Commercial PPO Program, and the secondary coverage only receives crossover or secondary claims.
- *A customer with an in-effect Original Medicare Part B record prefers to pay cash for a Medicare-covered dressing. Can the program be placed on the Wound Care Self-Pay Program?* No; that customer is enrolled on the Wound Care Original Medicare Program.
- *Does a change of insurance change the program's status?* No; a program change rewrites the coverage reference and the tier together and never rewrites status.
